# PD-1 Inhibitor Resistance — ACME Q3 2026 Update

## Background
PD-1 inhibitor resistance remains a critical challenge in melanoma and NSCLC.
Approximately 40-60% of initial responders develop acquired resistance within 2 years.
This Q3 update revisits mechanisms with new data from ASCO 2026.

## Mechanism of Action
PD-1 binds to PD-L1 expressed on tumor cells, delivering an inhibitory signal that
attenuates T-cell receptor signaling. New 2026 data implicates SETDB1 loss as a driver
of innate resistance via endogenous retrovirus suppression. Loss of antigen presentation
(B2M loss) and JAK1/JAK2 mutations remain dominant acquired-resistance mechanisms.

## Biomarkers of Resistance
TMB, MSI, and IFN-gamma signatures correlate with response.
NEW: Tertiary lymphoid structures (TLS) density now validated as a positive predictor in melanoma.

## Trials in Progress
KEYNOTE-789 readout occurred Q2 2026 (negative for OS in EGFR+ NSCLC).
CheckMate-9DW continues. RELATIVITY-047 update at ASCO 2026 confirmed durable PFS benefit.
NEW: KEYNOTE-D77 (pembro + ATR inhibitor) and IMmotion-LITE (atezo + CTLA4) active.

## Safety Signals
Immune-related adverse events (irAEs) include pneumonitis (3-5%), colitis (8-12%),
and endocrinopathies. Triple combinations now showing concerning grade 5 hepatitis signal — monitor closely.

## Strategic Implications
ASCO data shifts the field toward biomarker-stratified combinations. ACME should pivot
enrollment toward TLS-positive cohorts and consider an ATR inhibitor partnership.
